DILG LEGAL OPINION NO.2å S. 2017 31 MAY 2017 FELIX A. SY, M.D. Municipal Mayor Manjuyod, Negros Oriental Dear Mayor Sy, This pertains to your letterl requesting the office of Secretary Ismael D. Sueno for an authority to practice your profession as a General Surgeon. Per your representation, you were a surgeon for over twenty years in a government hospital prior to your election as Municipal Mayor and you intend to continue helping patients especially in the poor community. Anent thereto, we wish to invite your attention to applicable provisions of Republic Act No. 71602 particularly Section 9 thereof which explicitly provides: "SECTION 90. Practice of Profession. — All governors, city and municipal are prehi&ited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation ether than the exercise Q/ their functions as chief executives. (b) Sanggunian members may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours: Provided, That sanggunian members who are also members of the Bar shall not: (I) Appear as counsel before any court in any civil case wherein a local government unit or any office, agency, or instrumentality of the government is the adverse party; January 9, 2017 The Local Government Code of 1991 1

(2) Appear as counsel in any criminal case wherein an officer or employee of the national or local government is accused of an offense committed in relation to his office. (3) Collect any fee for their appearance in administrative proceedings involving the local government unit of which he is an official; and (4) Use property and personnel of the government except when the sanggunian member concerned is defending the interest of the government. (G) Doctors Of medicine practice their profession even n/ f wor ffi i lh ur n i il : Prov i ns n derive monetary compensation therefrom." (Emphasis ours) Governors and mayors of cities and municipalities are prohibited from practicing their professions or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. The reason is that the office of the governor or mayor is a full time job. To allow the governor or the mayor to practice a profession, say as a lawyer, doctor or engineer, may give rise to a conflict of interest. The governor or the mayor may be tempted to devote more time to the practice of his profession than to the discharge of the duties of his office.3 This Department has consistently opined that this prohibition is absolute.4 It bears emphasizing that pursuant to paragraph (c) of the aforequoted provisions, you as a doctor is allowed to practice your profession even during official hours of work only on occasions of emergency: provided, that you do not derive monetary compensation therefrom. The correlated provisions of Republic Act No. 67135 specifically Section 7 thereof is likewise emphatic as it provides: "Section 7. Prohibited acts and transactions. — In addition to acts and omissions of public officials and employees now prescribed in the Constitution and existing laws, the following shall constitute prohibited acts and transactions 3 Aquilino Q. Pimentel, Jr., The Local Government Code of 1991: The Key to National Development, Page 204, 1993 Edition. DILG Legal Opinion NOS. 26, S. 2013, dated August 7, 2013 and 101 S. 2007, dated November 7, 2007 s Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees 2

of any public official and employee and are hereby declared to be unlawful: "(b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto.-Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: Xxx xxx xxx (2) Enqaqe in the private practice Qf their profession unless authorized by the Constitution or law. provided that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their Qfficipl functions;" (Emphasis supplied) Verily, your concern herein as a municipal mayor unambiguously falls under the above-referred provisions of law. Therefore, you are prohibited from practicing your profession as a doctor except, as emphasized, on occasions of emergency. In view of the foregoing, though we may be readily persuaded by your noble intention to help your needy constituents via the practice of your medical profession, perforce, this Department cannot validly grant your request. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Assistant Secretary Enclosure: as stated LLLS/TID,'78 3
